cpu_source: the cpuTime of each invocation in `wrangler tail domains-probe --format json`, joined by the call label; a fetch answer carries no CPU time

route.summary:
one Fetch v4 of topic= (partition=

, default 0) at offset= over a TCP socket to kafka.zonestream.openintel.nl:9092, at most max_bytes (default 1048576, cap 67108864); sockets=<1..6> opens that many at once; 30000 ms of wall time; answers messages, bytes, next_offset and decode_ms

definitions.offset: the offset the read starts at: the query's own number, or the one ListOffsets v1 gave for earliest, latest, latest-N (clamped at the earliest) or a time (the first message at or after it, the latest offset when there is none)
definitions.messages: the records at or after offset in the whole batches of the answer that decoded; control records excluded
definitions.bytes: the Fetch v4 response as it came off the socket, its 4-byte size included
definitions.wire_bytes: the whole batches whose offsets reach offset or past it, exactly as the broker returned them, still compressed: the bytes a raw lane stores
definitions.raw_bytes: the record values counted in messages, after decoding
definitions.decoded_bytes: the counted batches that decoded, after decompression, 61-byte batch headers included
definitions.next_offset: one past the last offset of the last counted batch, decoded or failed; offset when the answer held no whole batch at or past it. Passed back as offset, it resumes the read with no gap and no repeat
definitions.lag: high_watermark - next_offset: the messages the partition held past this answer
definitions.partial_bytes: the bytes of a batch the broker cut at the size limit, at the end of the answer; it is read again from next_offset
definitions.failed_batches: counted batches that did not decode, by kind in failures: crc (CRC-32C mismatch), snappy, codec (a codec this route does not decode), records (records that do not match the header), magic, truncated
definitions.decode_ms: the Worker's clock across the split and the decode. Deployed, the clock advances only after I/O, so a decode reads 0 (Cloudflare's documentation); locally it advances regardless. The CPU time is in Workers Logs and `wrangler tail`, not in this answer
definitions.ms: the Worker's clock across each stage: connect (every socket opened or failed), api_versions, list_offsets (null when offset is a number), fetch (request written to response read), wall (the whole call)
definitions.cpu_ms: the invocation's cpuTime in its `wrangler tail --format json` event, joined to the call by the call label in its URL; null when the tail gave no event or no cpuTime
definitions.tail_wall_ms: the invocation's wallTime in the same event
definitions.outcome: the invocation's outcome in the same event: ok, exception, exceededCpu, exceededMemory, canceled, ...
definitions.client_ms: the wall time of the call as this script saw it, from the request to the end of the answer
definitions.topics.seconds: the sum of client_ms over the loop calls of the topic
definitions.topics.mb_per_second: bytes / seconds / 1e6 (bytes off the broker socket)
definitions.topics.cpu.full_calls: the loop calls of the topic that answered 200 with messages and a lag above 0 after them: the answer ended before the head (at max_bytes, or at the end of a log segment), so the call read from a backlog
definitions.topics.cpu.per_1000_ms: the sum of cpu_ms over the full calls with a figure, divided by their messages, times 1,000: the figure the pass rule judges
definitions.topics.cpu.p50_per_1000_ms: the quantile at index floor(n * q) of the ascending cpu_ms / messages * 1000 of each full call with a figure (probes/worker/src/gaps.ts quantile); p99 and max the same
definitions.topics.cpu.all_per_1000_ms: the same sum over every loop call with a figure, the calls at the head included: what a lane that reads at the head pays
definitions.topics.cpu.empty_call_cpu_ms: the cpu_ms of the calls that read no message: the fixed cost of an invocation that opens a socket and asks once
definitions.sweep.largest_ok_max_bytes: the largest max_bytes of the sweep whose call answered 200
